newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols soften as spot pulls back.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/mark vols soften as spot pulls back.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark options softened in U.S. trading as the spot greenback pulled back a full pfennig after jumping to a six-year high of 1.84 marks earlier, dealers said.

"We're in a trend, so people are pretty much prepared -- not 'well prepared' because obviously vols are still pretty well bid, but pretty much prepared -- to see the dollar keep going," said a U.S. bank trader in the West Coast.
"Consequently, only accelerations (of the dollar's advances) are likely to cause vols to come up further," he said.
Earlier, volatilities briefly firmed as the dollar touched 1.8400 marks after the Bundesbank policy council left German interest rates unchanged. But they recoiled as spot retreated.
The dollar/mark volatility curve was virtually flat at about 10.3/10.6 percent from one-month out to one-year at U.S. midsession, off a quarter point on the day in one-month.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal, the put/call pricing differential, barely moved at 0.5/0.8 percentage point skewed for mark puts.
"It's unchanged from yesterday, so it's also telling you that the market is not panicking," the West Coast trader said.
Traders said talk of exotic option triggers in the 1.8450-1.8550 mark area and higher might be one factor holding down volatilities despite the fairly big daily spot movements.
Dealers who had sold exotics like double-knockouts to end-users typically hedge their theta exposure by selling short-dated plain vanilla options.

On the other hand, a choppy volatility market may lie ahead because as spot continues to rise and the triggers are taken out, those vanilla option positions suddenly become naked, causing short-covering for gamma. Shorter-dated options have higher theta as well as gamma.
"Even though front-end vols are soft, it doesn't mean there's any real temptation to sell gamma," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
Traders said some sizable exotic options with trigger prices at 2.0 marks had been traded.
"Be it trigger or strike price, everyone in the market is starting to look at the 2.0-mark level," Okada said.

He added that anticipation of further dollar strength against European currencies was spurring large long-dated French franc put buying through 25-35 delta risk-reversals in the nine-month to one-year maturities.
Dollar/yen volatilities were weaker as spot continued chopping back and forth within familiar ranges, sandwiched between a bullish dollar/mark and bearish mark/yen.
One-month dollar/yen volatility fell by half a point to 9.65/9.85 percent.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal was at 0.4/0.7 in favor of yen calls.

"It's still bid for yen calls, but directionality views in the market have become less one-sided," Okada said. "We're seeing more interest in the upside strikes like 118-119 yen, and yen puts are now priced above at-the-money."
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
